en.name: Tomato paste
en.summary: An unopened can or tube of tomato paste keeps 27 months from purchase in the cupboard. Once opened it is a refrigerated food with 5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 2–3 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: Cool, dry and dark, 27 months from purchase — an unusually long figure, and it comes from the combination of a high-acid product, a heavy heat process and a sealed can or tube. Keep cans off damp floors and away from the hob, and rotate them so the oldest is used first. A can that is bulging, leaking, rusted through or badly dented on a seam goes in the bin unopened and untasted. A tube is easier to live with than a can precisely because you never have to open the whole thing at once.
en.fridge: Opened, tomato paste keeps 5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Leftovers do not need to leave the can for safety, but they should for flavour — an open can gives the paste a metallic edge and the surface dries into a dark skin within a day. Scrape it into a small covered container, level the surface and pour a thin film of olive oil over it to keep air off. An opened tube keeps in the fridge with the cap on and the nozzle wiped clean.
en.freezer: 2–3 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and this is the right answer for the tablespoon-at-a-time problem. Spoon the leftover paste into an ice cube tray, freeze it solid, then transfer the cubes to a bag — each cube is roughly what a sauce needs, and they go straight from the freezer into a hot pan. Tomato paste freezes better than almost anything else in this category because it is already concentrated, so there is little water to form damaging ice crystals.
en.thawing: There is no need to thaw: drop a frozen cube straight into a hot pan or a simmering sauce. If you must thaw it, do it in the fridge, never on the counter.
spoilage: A bulging, leaking or badly dented can, or one that spurts when opened.
Mould on the surface of an opened container, often white or blue-green.
A fermented, yeasty or fizzy character rather than a clean tomato smell.
Paste that has darkened to brown-black and dried hard, or gone watery and separated.
tips: Freeze leftovers in an ice cube tray on the day you open the can.
Cover refrigerated paste with a film of olive oil to keep air off.
Buy tubes if you use paste a spoonful at a time.
Never store an opened can; decant into a covered container.

faq.q: How long does tomato paste last after opening?
faq.a: 5 days in a covered container in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 2–3 months frozen at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 2–3 months. Freeze it in an ice cube tray and drop the cubes straight into a hot pan — no thawing needed.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep leftover paste in the can?
faq.a: It is safe, but it picks up a metallic taste and dries out. Move it to a covered container or freeze it.

zh.name: 番茄糊
zh.summary: 未開封的番茄糊罐頭或軟管，從購買日起算放櫥櫃可放 27 個月。一開封它就是冷藏食品：4 °C 以下 5 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 2～3 個月。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、乾燥、避光，自購買日起 27 個月——這是個相當長的數字，它來自三件事的組合：高酸性的產品、強度足夠的加熱製程，以及完好的密封罐或軟管。罐頭不要放在潮濕地面，也要遠離爐台，並且輪替使用、先用舊的。罐身膨脹、滲漏、鏽穿或接縫嚴重凹陷的，請不要打開、不要試吃，直接丟棄。軟管包裝比罐頭好用，理由正是你不必一次把整份都打開。
zh.fridge: 開封後，番茄糊在 4 °C 以下可放 5 天。剩下的就安全而言不一定要離開罐子，但為了味道應該離開——開過的罐子會讓番茄糊帶金屬味，表面也會在一天內乾成一層深色的皮。請刮進小的加蓋容器，把表面抹平，再淋一層薄薄的橄欖油隔絕空氣。軟管則蓋好蓋子、擦乾淨管口後冷藏即可。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 2～3 個月，而這正是「每次只用一大匙」這個難題的正解。把剩下的番茄糊舀進製冰盒，凍硬後倒進保鮮袋——一格差不多就是一鍋醬需要的量，而且可以從冷凍直接下熱鍋。番茄糊大概是這一類食材裡最耐冷凍的，因為它本來就是濃縮品，水分少，冰晶造成的破壞也小。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍：把冷凍的番茄糊方塊直接丟進熱鍋或滾著的醬汁裡。真的要解凍就放冷藏，不要放室溫。
spoilage: 罐身膨脹、滲漏或嚴重凹陷，或開罐時噴汁。
開封後的容器表面長霉，常見白色或藍綠色。
有發酵味、酵母味或氣泡感，而不是乾淨的番茄味。
顏色變成褐黑並乾硬，或整個變得水水的、分層。
tips: 開罐當天就把剩料倒進製冰盒冷凍。
冷藏的番茄糊表面淋一層橄欖油隔絕空氣。
每次只用一匙的人，買軟管包裝。
絕對不要整罐開著冰，請換到加蓋容器。

faq.q: 番茄糊開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 換到加蓋容器放 4 °C 以下冷藏 5 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 2～3 個月。
可以，2～3 個月。用製冰盒分格冷凍，之後直接下熱鍋，不必解凍。

faq.q: 剩下的可以留在罐子裡嗎？
faq.a: 安全上可以，但會帶金屬味也會乾掉。請換到加蓋容器或直接冷凍。
